conversation.user: I am an international applicant interested in the Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Technician Certificate. Is it available to international applicants?
conversation.advisor:
No. The **Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Technician Certificate** is **not available to international students**.

The program is a full-time, in-person certificate offered at the Burnaby Campus. The program page states that scheduled intakes are subject to change and that applications are accepted throughout the year, subject to space.

For details, visit the [program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/heating-ventilation-air-conditioning-and-refrigeration-technician-certificate-full-time-2958cert/).

For more information, see BCIT International Students: https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/.

conversation.user: So does that automatically mean I'm admitted?
conversation.advisor:
No. Meeting the entrance requirements—or being considered a qualified applicant—does **not automatically mean you have been admitted**.

For the **Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Technician Certificate**, applicants are accepted on a first-qualified basis only while space remains; otherwise, qualified applicants may be wait-listed. The program record also states that it is **not available to international students**.

Your official application status should be checked through your **myBCIT/myCommunication** account. [View the program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/heating-ventilation-air-conditioning-and-refrigeration-technician-certificate-full-time-2958cert/).

expectation.question: So does that automatically mean I'm admitted?
expectation.expected: No. Separate international availability from individual admission, competition, and human verification. Do not guarantee admission.

conversation.user: What can you actually verify, and what should I confirm with BCIT?
conversation.advisor:
Based on the available BCIT program information, I can verify the following for the **Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Technician Certificate**:

### What is verified

- The program is **active**, **full-time**, delivered **in person** at the **Burnaby Campus**.
- It is a **certificate program** lasting approximately **41 weeks**.
- The program is recorded as **not available to international students**.
- The stated entrance requirements include:
  - English Studies 12 or an accepted equivalent, typically **67%**, or the BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment.
  - One accepted Grade 11 mathematics option, typically **60%**, or the BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment.
  - The **BCIT Mechanical Reasoning Trades Entry Assessment**.
- Applicants must meet the entrance requirements before applying.
- Qualified applicants are accepted on a **first-qualified basis while space remains**. If an intake is full, qualified applicants may be wait-listed.
- The curriculum record contains **23 required courses totaling 84.5 credits**.
- The program information says scheduled intakes are generally in **September**, but schedules may change. Applications are described as accepted throughout the year.

### What I cannot verify about you

I cannot verify:

- Whether BCIT has accepted or admitted you.
- Whether your specific education, grades, English ability, mathematics background, or assessments satisfy BCIT’s requirements.
- Whether your documents or international status have been reviewed and accepted.
- Whether space remains in a particular intake.
- Whether you are currently wait-listed.
- Your application status or any decision in your myBCIT/myCommunication account.

### What to confirm directly with BCIT

Please confirm with BCIT:

1. Whether you are eligible to apply as an international applicant, since the program record currently states that it is not available to international students.
2. Whether a particular credential, course, or assessment from your country is accepted as equivalent.
3. Whether the program is open for the intake you want and whether space remains.
4. Whether your application has been received, is complete, or is wait-listed.
5. Your official admission decision through **myBCIT/myCommunication**.

The program record says BCIT sends application correspondence through myCommunication and that applicants should monitor their BCIT email and account. You can also review the program page here:

[BCIT HVAC and R Technician Certificate](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/heating-ventilation-air-conditioning-and-refrigeration-technician-certificate-full-time-2958cert/)

I would treat BCIT’s admissions office and your myBCIT account as the final sources for your individual eligibility and admission status.

programs.program_name: Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Technician
programs.program_overview: The Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVAC and R) Technician certificate is a non co-op program which provides a foundation in heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration system design, installation and service. industry designs, builds, maintains and repairs essential indoor comfort and cooling systems. Delivery: in person. See details . As a result of the expanding markets for refrigeration and air conditioning and changing technology, a dramatic need exists for qualified personnel both at home and abroad. Refrigeration equipment is used in supermarkets, and food processing and cold storage facilities, and sports facilities such as hockey and curling rinks, which are also a vital part of the industry. A Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Mechanic journeyperson fabricates, installs, alters, repairs/services any system used for cooling and/or heating (e.g. heat pumps) in closed systems that contain a refrigerant or a brine and thermoelectric cooling. This includes piping, controls and electrical work. These workers also connect rooftop units to gas and test and balance systems. The program The HVAC and R Technician certificate program is 41 weeks in duration combining classroom and shop instruction. After learning direct refrigeration systems, a broad range of topics focused on HVAC systems design, operation and controls are learned. Emphasis will be placed on diagnosis, service requirements and procedures. The first two levels of Gas B training is also included. (level 2 & 3). Who it’s for This career path is suited to those who are interested in designing, building, maintaining and repairing essential indoor comfort and cooling systems and who enjoy being independent, troubleshooting and and problem solving. What grads can do Graduates of this program who enter the trade within one year of graduation can expect to receive credit for three levels of technical training for the Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Mechanic apprenticeship. Students are encouraged to return to Level 4 apprentice training (10 weeks) when appropriate to complete their level 4 training to qualify to write their Gas B ticket and prepare for the Interprovincial Red Seal certification exam. Next up Entrance Requirements
programs.notes: Program length 41 weeks, full-time Grading The course passing grade is 64 per cent. In order to successfully complete each level, a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 70 per cent is required. An overall GPA of 70 per cent is required to successfully complete the program. Accreditation Graduates of this program who enter the trade within one year of graduation can expect to receive credit for three levels of technical training for the Refrigeration and Air Conditioning apprenticeship. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Industry training authority BCIT transfers the student's name, contact information, Personal Education Number (PEN), and the name and date of the completed Foundation program to SkilledTradesBC. This information is used for the purposes of tracking successful completions in order to grant credit towards apprenticeship where applicable, and communicating with trainees to promote continuation in an apprenticeship program. Delivery: in person. See details . As a result of the expanding markets for refrigeration and air conditioning and changing technology, a dramatic need exists for qualified personnel both at home and abroad. Refrigeration equipment is used in supermarkets, and food processing and cold storage facilities, and sports facilities such as hockey and curling rinks, which are also a vital part of the industry. A Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Mechanic journeyperson fabricates, installs, alters, repairs/services any system used for cooling and/or heating (e.g. heat pumps) in closed systems that contain a refrigerant or a brine and thermoelectric cooling. This includes piping, controls and electrical work. These workers also connect rooftop units to gas and test and balance systems. The program The HVAC and R Technician certificate program is 41 weeks in duration combining classroom and shop instruction. After learning direct refrigeration systems, a broad range of topics focused on HVAC systems design, operation and controls are learned. Emphasis will be placed on diagnosis, service requirements and procedures. The first two levels of Gas B training is also included. (level 2 & 3). Who it’s for This career path is suited to those who are interested in designing, building, maintaining and repairing essential indoor comfort and cooling systems and who enjoy being independent, troubleshooting and and problem solving. What grads can do Graduates of this program who enter the trade within one year of graduation can expect to receive credit for three levels of technical training for the Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Mechanic apprenticeship. Students are encouraged to return to Level 4 apprentice training (10 weeks) when appropriate to complete their level 4 training to qualify to write their Gas B ticket and prepare for the Interprovincial Red Seal certification exam. Next up Entrance Requirements

Based on the available BCIT program information, I can verify the following for the **Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Technician Certificate**:

### What is verified

- The program is **active**, **full-time**, delivered **in person** at the **Burnaby Campus**.
- It is a **certificate program** lasting approximately **41 weeks**.
- The program is recorded as **not available to international students**.
- The stated entrance requirements include:
  - English Studies 12 or an accepted equivalent, typically **67%**, or the BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment.
  - One accepted Grade 11 mathematics option, typically **60%**, or the BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment.
  - The **BCIT Mechanical Reasoning Trades Entry Assessment**.
- Applicants must meet the entrance requirements before applying.
- Qualified applicants are accepted on a **first-qualified basis while space remains**. If an intake is full, qualified applicants may be wait-listed.
- The curriculum record contains **23 required courses totaling 84.5 credits**.
- The program information says scheduled intakes are generally in **September**, but schedules may change. Applications are described as accepted throughout the year.

### What I cannot verify about you

I cannot verify:

- Whether BCIT has accepted or admitted you.
- Whether your specific education, grades, English ability, mathematics background, or assessments satisfy BCIT’s requirements.
- Whether your documents or international status have been reviewed and accepted.
- Whether space remains in a particular intake.
- Whether you are currently wait-listed.
- Your application status or any decision in your myBCIT/myCommunication account.

### What to confirm directly with BCIT

Please confirm with BCIT:

1. Whether you are eligible to apply as an international applicant, since the program record currently states that it is not available to international students.
2. Whether a particular credential, course, or assessment from your country is accepted as equivalent.
3. Whether the program is open for the intake you want and whether space remains.
4. Whether your application has been received, is complete, or is wait-listed.
5. Your official admission decision through **myBCIT/myCommunication**.

The program record says BCIT sends application correspondence through myCommunication and that applicants should monitor their BCIT email and account. You can also review the program page here:

[BCIT HVAC and R Technician Certificate](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/heating-ventilation-air-conditioning-and-refrigeration-technician-certificate-full-time-2958cert/)

I would treat BCIT’s admissions office and your myBCIT account as the final sources for your individual eligibility and admission status.

conditions.description: Note: This trade program is in high demand. Visit Trades Training BC to estimate a future start date. Scheduled intakes September each year. *Scheduled intakes are subject to change Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program. If you are uncertain or don’t meet the requirements we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. English language proficiency: one of the following: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment Math: one of the following: Pre-Calculus 11 (60%) or Foundations of Math 11 (60%) or Workplace Math 11 (60%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment BCIT Mechanical Reasoning Trades Entry Assessment Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Trades Discovery The Trades Discovery General and Trades Discovery for Women are full-time programs designed to prepare participants to successfully enter and complete a Trades Training program. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
